title: Communist Climb
description: In this image taken in 1987, young Communists rest at the summit of Rysy—the highest peak in Poland, standing at 8,199 feet. Husband-and-wife photographers John Eastcott and Yva Momatiuk documented the climb that commemorated Vladimir Lenin's supposed ascent while in exile in 1913, just years before he founded the Soviet Union. Rysy is part of the High Tatras mountain range, which at the time was located on Poland's border with Czechoslovakia, a country under the Soviet sphere of influence until it was dissolved into the Czech Republic and Slovakia in 1992.
translated_description: 这张拍摄于1987年的照片中，年轻的共产主义者在波兰最高峰雷瑟峰（海拔8199英尺）的山顶休憩。摄影师约翰·伊斯科特与伊娃·莫马蒂乌克夫妇记录下这次登山活动——该活动旨在纪念弗拉基米尔·列宁1913年流亡期间曾攀登此峰的传说，而数年后他便创立了苏联。雷瑟峰属于高塔特拉山脉，当时正位于波兰与捷克斯洛伐克边境。这个国家长期处于苏联势力范围内，直至1992年解体为捷克共和国和斯洛伐克。
